transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-04
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Mark Enders (CISO, Cedar Bank), Lisa Wu (VP Eng), Carlos Ramos (Platform)

Summary: quick security review focused on audit logs and admin activity for Cedar Bank's planned pilot. Discussed what events are captured, retention/export options, encryption and KMS integration, RBAC and SSO considerations, and next steps for SOC2 artifacts and exports.

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm alex from redwood, and priya's here from our security and infra team. how's everyone doing?
[00:05] Mark: good, thanks. we've got about forty minutes. want to focus on audit logging and what we'll need for the pilot, specifically retention and export to our S3.
[00:12] Alex: perfect, that's what we planned to cover. priya, you wanna kick off with the high-level of what we capture?
[00:16] Priya: sure. so, in Redwood our audit logs are two main buckets — admin activity and data access. admin activity includes things like user creation/deletion, role changes, RBAC policy edits, SSO/SAML configuration changes, API key generation/revocation, model rollout events, and configuration changes to dedicated or private deployments. data access logs are, e.g., request-level meta — who called the API, endpoint, model used, token counts, and latency.
[00:41] Lisa: when you say model rollout events can you be specific? like if we do a canary switch, is that logged?
[00:45] Priya: yes, canary rollouts, A/B switches, model version pins — all of that is recorded with the actor (redwood user or service account) and the timestamp. sometimes the transcription splices names, so to clarify we include the request context id and the change diff where appropriate.
[01:00] Carlos: any PII in those logs? we need to minimize exposure, especially for payment workflows.
[01:04] Priya: good question. we purposely avoid storing full user prompts in admin logs. request-level logs capture metadata and hashes/prefix fingerprints of inputs for debugging, but not full prompt text unless you enable debug logging in a support/TAC flow. For PCI or PII-sensitive orgs we recommend redwood private with data residency and strict debug opt-in.
[01:20] Mark: ok, and retention — by default how long do you keep logs?
[01:23] Alex: our default hosted retention is 30 days for detailed request logs and 365 days for high-level admin audit events, but for enterprise customers we support configurable retention windows. priya, correct on the tiers?
[01:33] Priya: yes. for cedar we can do a 90-day detailed retention policy for request-level logs and extended 1-year admin events if that's your preference; also you can export logs to your S3 for long-term archival. there are tradeoffs around storage costs and egress.
[01:47] Lisa: export options — can we push to our bank-managed S3 and also stream to our SIEM (splunk/elastic)?
[01:53] Priya: yes. we support scheduled batch exports to S3 (parquet or csv), real-time streaming via secure webhook or syslog connector for Splunk, and direct cloud forwarders for BigQuery/Elastic with options for signed, encrypted transfers. for private deployments we can also write directly to your internal logging cluster.
[02:09] Carlos: about encryption — are exported files encrypted at rest with our KMS? we need logs encrypted with our customer-managed keys.
[02:15] Priya: we support server-side encryption with customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS for S3 exports. for hosted exports we can either push encrypted blobs to your bucket using your KMS, or for private deployments you can handle encryption end-to-end. also all logs are encrypted in transit with TLS.
[02:29] Mark: does Redwood ever have plaintext access to the exported logs?
[02:32] Alex: we don't retain a copy of your exported archive beyond the transfer window. for hosted we may buffer for a short period during delivery; those buffers are encrypted and access-controlled. if you want zero-retention on Redwood's side we can set up direct pushes to your bucket with minimal buffering, or choose Private where you keep everything on-prem.
[02:49] Lisa: audit log schema — what fields are included? we need user id, role, ip, action, resource id, old/new values, correlation id — do you have those?
[02:58] Priya: yes, typical fields: event_time, actor_id, actor_role, actor_source_ip, action_type, resource_type, resource_id, before_state (truncated), after_state (truncated), request_id, correlation_id, service_component, and optional metadata like model_version and region. we'll send a sample CSV/parquet schema.
[03:24] Carlos: and for admin actions like key rotation, does it log KMS key id?
[03:28] Priya: we log the event (key_rotated) and the key identifier reference, but we don't log the secret material. we also log who performed the rotation and any affected resources.
[03:37] Mark: SSO and RBAC — if we provision via SCIM/SAML and do role changes from our IdP, does Redwood's audit show both origin (IdP) and resulting local state?
[03:46] Alex: yes, we record the origin and attribute the actor; it might show as service-account:scim-sync or your IdP user depending on how you configure SCIM just to be explicit.
[03:54] Lisa: do you have immutable logs or write-once buckets? compliance sometimes asks for WORM capability.
[03:58] Priya: for exported archives we can write to your S3 with object lock enabled if you request WORM. Redwood's internal audit store is append-only but not a certified WORM; for the high-assurance requirement we advise bank-managed bucket with object-lock and retention policies.
[04:15] Mark: how about alerting on suspicious admin activity? can logs trigger webhook alerts or send to SIEM rule engine?
[04:20] Priya: yes, we support configurable alerts on events like unusual API key creation, mass role changes, or out-of-hours admin logins. Alerts can be sent to webhooks, PagerDuty, or your SIEM.
[04:29] Alex: just to call out, we also surface change diffs on config updates in the console and include them in the audit trail so you can see 'before' and 'after'.
[04:36] Lisa: any PII in the 'before/after' states? need to redact certain fields automatically.
[04:40] Priya: we can redact sensitive fields by default; we maintain a mapping where common sensitive keys are masked. if you have custom fields, we can add them to the redact list during onboarding.
[04:50] Carlos: for the pilot, we'll need a sample export with 30 days of synthetic data to validate our SIEM parsing. can you provide that?
[04:56] Alex: yes, we'll provide a sanitized sample export (CSV/parquet) that matches the schema. action item noted.
[05:00] Mark: legal also asked about chain of custody for logs — any signatures or hash verification?
[05:05] Priya: exported archives can be checksummed with SHA256 and we can provide signed manifests. for stronger requirements we can provide an HMAC-signed manifest tied to the transfer.
[05:15] Lisa: curious about cost — is there an egress or export fee for pushing to our S3?
[05:19] Alex: for hosted customers there's a small egress fee tied to the export volume; we can model estimates based on expected log volumes. for dedicated/private deployments, typically it's part of the contract. we'll include a rough cost estimate in the follow-up.
[05:29] Mark: can you support role-based retention? e.g., all admin events retained longer than per-request logs for 12 months, while request logs drop after 90 days.
[05:36] Priya: yes, retention tiers by event type are configurable per account. we can align admin audit events to 12 months and request-level logs to 90 days as you requested.
[05:44] Alex: quick note on debug logs — if we enable full debug for a troubleshooting run, those logs might include prompt text; those are only enabled via explicit support tickets and access is restricted.
[05:54] Mark: good. last question: are logs correlated with tenant and region? we need to ensure logs for EU data stay in region if we choose data residency.
[06:01] Priya: logs include region tags. for data residency we can configure exports to a region-bound bucket; for private deployments the logs stay within your VPC/region.
[06:12] Lisa: ok that covers most of it. recap of next steps?
[06:15] Alex: i'll send SOC2 docs and the sanitized sample export. priya will send the schema and KMS integration notes. we'll schedule a follow-up demo to show private deployment networking and export flow. carlos to confirm retention requirements on your side.
[06:28] Mark: perfect, thanks everyone.
[06:30] (meeting wraps; small side chat continues briefly)

End of transcript.
